title: Allight: A Perfect Photon Collector
authors: Dan Porat, Ran Finkelstein, Tal Carmon
abstract: Collecting photons from quantum emitters remains a key limitation in light-matter interaction because conventional lenses collect light only from one direction. Here, we introduce a perfect light collector by inverse-designing a surrounding dielectric structure that encloses the emitter to increase photon-collection efficiency toward unity. Decomposing the device into several refractive interfaces enables emission collection from the full 4$π$ solid angle with adiabatic reshaping into a collimated beam. We experimentally demonstrate, in two dimensions, the ray bending that collimates omnidirectional emission. Our collector transforms current paradigms for highly efficient photon collection from narrowband, cavity-based techniques into experimentally robust, broadband, non-resonant dielectric devices.
summary: This paper introduces 'Allight,' a novel, broadband dielectric structure designed to overcome the fundamental limitation of photon collection from quantum emitters. By inverse-designing multiple refractive interfaces, the structure redirects light emitted over the full 4pi solid angle into a highly collimated beam. This breakthrough promises to significantly enhance the efficiency of quantum interconnects and remote entanglement distribution.
main_problem: Efficiently collecting photons from quantum emitters is severely limited by conventional optics, which only capture light from a narrow direction.
main_result: The proposed 'Allight' structure achieves near-unity photon collection efficiency by adiabatically reshaping omnidirectional emission into a collimated beam.
method: The structure is designed using an inverse-design algorithm that iteratively shapes multiple dielectric interfaces based on Snell's law to redirect all emitted rays.
model_or_system: The system is a surrounding dielectric structure designed to enclose a quantum emitter, enabling collection from the full 4pi solid angle into a collimated beam. Prototypes have been fabricated in 2D using polycarbonate and tested with laser beams.
key_observables: Photon-collection efficiency ($\eta$), beam collimation, and residual scattering patterns.
important_parameters: Near-unity efficiency, full 4pi solid angle collection, broadband/non-resonant operation, and fabrication tolerances ($\lambda/2$ error).
main_assumptions: The design assumes the ability to fabricate multiple dielectric interfaces with high precision, and that antireflection coatings maintain high transmission.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the collector design, ray tracing through multiple interfaces, the 2D experimental proof-of-concept, and the theoretical framework for the inverse-design algorithm.
paper_structure: The paper details the physical limitation, introduces the inverse-design methodology (using ray tracing and Snell's law), presents experimental validation on a 2D prototype, and analyzes the robustness against fabrication errors.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses a critical hardware bottleneck—efficient photon coupling—for scaling quantum networks and quantum computing architectures that rely on photonic interconnects.
